correctness.rationale: For vertices e_i+f_j of standard simplex product, a generic functional has additive scores p_i+q_j. Its top two scores must differ in only one index; conversely every ordered distinct same-row or same-column pair is forced as the top two by making the untouched factor score gap sufficiently large. The source vertex-lineup criterion therefore yields exactly de(e-1)+de(d-1)=de(d+e-2) distinct vertices for alpha>beta>0. Each occupation vector has squared norm 1+alpha^2+beta^2 and row/column coordinate sums 1, so its squared distance from c=(1/d 1_d,1/e 1_e) is R^2=1+alpha^2+beta^2-1/d-1/e. The de cyclic same-row contact vertices have average c (both alpha and beta visit each column once per row). For any candidate center q their average squared distance is R^2+||q-c||^2; hence every other center requires radius strictly >R, proving exact uniqueness and that all vertices are contacts. All d,e>=2 and admissible alpha,beta follow algebraically; exact rational checker finite d,e<=8 is not extrapolated.
